note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Uganda: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident pays nothing on the first UGX 4,020,000 of annual chargeable income, then 20% to 4,920,000, 25% to 5,820,000, 30% to 120 million and 40% above; there is no regional income tax.
figures.applies: Year of income from 1 July 2026 (page reviewed 22 October 2026).

figures.finding: The year of income runs 1 July to 30 June; the return is due within six months of its end, and provisional tax is paid in four 25% instalments in the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th months.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year runs from 1 July through 30 June.
All taxpayers are obligated to file a return within six months of the end of the year of income.
Each instalment is 25% of the individual's estimate of tax due for that year.

figures.finding: The employee pays 5% and the employer 10% of gross pay to the National Social Security Fund.
figures.applies: 2026; the self-employed were not covered in the sources read.

sources.said: An individual in employment is obligated to make a contribution of 5% of one’s gross earnings to the national social security fund.
o make contributions to the national social security fund for each employee, amounting to 10% of their gross pay.

figures.finding: From 1 July 2026 anyone who pays a resident public entertainer withholds 6% of the gross payment, whatever the amount; the employer withholds PAYE from pay.

sources.said: Effective 1 July 2026, a 6% WHT applies on on a gross payment made to a resident public entertainer. This means that any person (whether designated as a withholding agent or not) who pays a public entertainer will be required to withhold tax at a rate of 6% on the gross payment irrespective of the amount paid.

figures.finding: A non-resident pays on Ugandan-source income from the first shilling: 10% to UGX 4,020,000, 20% to 4,920,000, 30% to 120 million and 40% above; royalties and management fees to a non-resident bear 15% withholding.
figures.applies: 2026/27; no separate non-resident entertainer rate was read.

WHT at a rate 15% therefore applies on gross dividend payments, interest, management fees, and royalty payments in respect of non-treaty countries.

figures.finding: VAT is 18%; a person must register once taxable supplies exceed UGX 37,500,000 in any three calendar months.

sources.said: The standard VAT rate is 18%; some items are zero rated and others are exempt.
a person is required to register for VAT if, within any period of three calendar months, one made taxable supplies exceeding UGX 37,500,000.
